stanzas: Uit die blou van onse hemel,
Uit die diepte van ons see,
Oor ons ewige gebergtes
Waar die kranse antwoord gee.
Deur ons vêr-verlate vlaktes
Met die kreun van ossewa –
Ruis die stem van ons geliefde,
Van ons land Suid-Afrika.
Ons sal antwoord op jou roepstem,
Ons sal offer wat jy vra:
Ons sal lewe, ons sal sterwe –
Ons vir jou, Suid-Afrika.
In die murg van ons gebeente,
In ons hart en siel en gees,
In ons roem op ons verlede,
In ons hoop op wat sal wees.
In ons wil en werk en wandel,
Van ons wieg tot aan ons graf –
Deel geen ander land ons liefde,
Trek geen ander trou ons af.
Vaderland! Ons sal die adel,
Van jou naam met ere dra:
Waar en trou as Afrikaners –
Kinders van Suid-Afrika.
In die songloed van ons somer,
In ons winternag se kou,
In die lente van ons liefde,
In die lanfer van ons rou.
By die klink van huw'liks-klokkies,
By die kluit-klap op die kis –
Streel jou stem ons nooit verniet nie,
Weet jy waar jou kinders is.
Op jou roep sê ons nooit nee nie,
Sê ons altyd, altyd ja:
Om te lewe, om te sterwe –
Ja, ons kom, Suid-Afrika.
Op U Almag vas vertrouend
Het ons vadere gebou:
Skenk ook ons die krag, o Here!
Om te handhaaf en te hou –
Dat die erwe van ons vad're
Vir ons kinders erwe bly:
Knegte van die Allerhoogste,
Teen die hele wêreld vry.
Soos ons vadere vertrou het,
Leer ook ons vertrou, o Heer –
Met ons land en met ons nasie
Sal dit wel wees, God regeer.
orig.credit: C. J. Langenhoven (1918); the Afrikaans text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: Out of the blue of our heaven,
out of the depth of our sea,
over our everlasting mountain ranges
where the cliffs give answer,
through our far-forsaken plains
with the groaning of the ox-wagon,
murmurs the voice of our beloved,
of our land South Africa.
We shall answer your call,
we shall offer what you ask:
we shall live, we shall die,
we for you, South Africa.
In the marrow of our bones,
in our heart and soul and spirit,
in our pride in our past,
in our hope for what will be,
in our will and work and way of life,
from our cradle to our grave,
no other land shares our love,
no other loyalty draws us away.
Fatherland! We shall bear the nobility
of your name with honour:
true and faithful as Afrikaners,
children of South Africa.
In the sun-glow of our summer,
in the cold of our winter night,
in the spring of our love,
in the crape of our mourning,
at the ringing of wedding bells,
at the thud of the clod on the coffin,
your voice never caresses us in vain,
you know where your children are.
To your call we never say no,
we always, always say yes:
to live, to die,
yes, we come, South Africa.
Firmly trusting in Your almighty power
our fathers built:
give us too the strength, O Lord,
to uphold and to keep,
that the heritage of our fathers
remain a heritage for our children:
servants of the Most High,
free against the whole world.
As our fathers trusted,
teach us too to trust, O Lord:
with our land and with our nation
it will be well, God reigns.

notes: line 1.7: 'ruis', to rustle, murmur or sound like the sea or wind.
line 2.5: 'wandel', one's walk, conduct, way of life.
line 2.8: 'Trek geen ander trou ons af', literally 'no other loyalty pulls us away'.
line 3.4: 'lanfer', black crape worn in mourning.
line 3.6: 'kluit-klap op die kis', the thud of clods of earth thrown on the coffin.
lines 4.5-4.6: 'erwe', inheritance, heritage (also plots of land).
